title: Il, lo, la: genere e articoli
summary: Nouns are masculine or feminine, the il/lo/la article choice, and how plurals flip the ending

blocks.title: Every noun has a gender
blocks.body: Italian nouns are **masculine** or **feminine** — even objects. A handy first rule from the ending: nouns in **-o** are usually masculine (*il libro*, book), nouns in **-a** usually feminine (*la casa*, house). Nouns in **-e** can be **either** — so you just learn the gender with the word (*il fiore* m, *la notte* f).
blocks.callout: Learn the article *with* the noun: not *casa* but *la casa*.

blocks.title: 'The' for masculine: il vs lo
blocks.body: Masculine 'the' is usually **il** (*il libro*, *il caffè*). But before tricky starts — **s+consonant, z, gn, ps, y** — it becomes **lo** (*lo studente*, *lo zaino*, *lo gnocco*). Before a vowel, both shrink to **l'** (*l'amico*). Feminine 'the' is **la**, or **l'** before a vowel (*la casa*, *l'amica*).

blocks.explain: *studente* starts with s+consonant, so masculine 'the' is *lo*: *lo studente*.

blocks.title: Plurals flip the vowel
blocks.body: To make a noun plural, change the **final vowel**, don't add -s. Masculine **-o → -i** (*libro → libri*). Feminine **-a → -e** (*casa → case*). Anything in **-e → -i**, whatever the gender (*studente → studenti*, *notte → notti*). The plural 'the' is *i* / *gli* (masc.) and *le* (fem.).

blocks.explain: Feminine -a → -e, and 'the' plural feminine is *le*: *le case*.
*I libri.* The noun flips -o → -i and the article *il* → *i*.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type. (It means 'the student', masculine.)
Pick four objects around you. Write each with its article (il/lo/la/l'), then make two of them plural. Guess the gender from the ending and check yourself.
